chief_complaint: Intermittent fever up to 39.5°C (103.1°F), night sweats, chest pain and fatigue.
history_of_present_illness: History of rheumatic fever in her childhood and mechanical mitral and aortic valve replacement at ages 37 and 53 years with St Jude Medical prostheses.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Visited relatives in Turkey several weeks before presentation.
vitals: Blood pressure and heart rate are within normal limits.
physical_exam: Unremarkable prosthetic heart sounds, systolic grade 1 murmur over aortic area without radiation, no enlarged liver or spleen, no palpable lymph nodes, no haemorrhages or petechiae.
labs_and_diagnostics: Slight anaemia (Hb 11.5g/dL), normal white blood cell count, lymphocyte-neutrophil ratio, and platelet count, C-reactive protein 15 mg/dL, normal serum creatinine and transaminases, negative blood cultures, urinary cultures yielded Enterobacteriaceae; chest radiography showed no infiltrates; transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated competent prosthetic valves.
differential_diagnosis: Urosepsis, brucellosis, tuberculosis, Q-fever, infective endocarditis.
management_and_clinical_course: Initially treated with co-trimoxazole for urinary tract infection, which improved fever but patient developed increasing dyspnoea and congestive heart failure. After 4 weeks, initial blood cultures grew Brucella melitensis biovar 2, and transoesophageal echocardiography revealed a large vegetation on the prosthetic mitral valve. Treatment with rifampicin, doxycycline, and gentamicin was initiated, leading to rapid improvement and normal C-reactive protein after 6 weeks. Two months later, an annular abscess cavity around the aortic prosthesis was found, leading to a third thoracotomy for prostheses exchange and eventual complete recovery.

images.caption: Transoesophageal echocardiography showing a two-cornered vegetation (arrow) measuring about 18mm × 7 mm attached to the posterolateral left atrial side of a St Jude Medical prosthesis in mitral position (LV, left ventricle; LA, left atrium).
